checklist.evidence: All diagnoses identify ConfigMap/vigil-app-nginx-config as the fault origin, matching the ground-truth target component.
The ConfigMap is identified as the origin, while Deployment/vigil-app and its container are described as downstream crash-looping victims.
No healthy component is blamed as the origin; the mem-load event in Diagnosis 3 is evidence, not its diagnosis.
Each diagnosis identifies an invalid nginx directive in the ConfigMap causing startup failure and vigil-app crash looping.
All diagnoses explicitly name the mutated directive `invalid_directive on;` and identify the affected nginx configuration template.
The diagnoses consistently attribute the failure to bad nginx configuration, with no conflicting or unrelated fault mechanism.
No uninvolved component is blamed; Deployment/vigil-app is correctly treated as affected by the faulty ConfigMap.
The diagnoses mention the faulty ConfigMap and affected vigil-app deployment, pods, or container, covering the ground-truth components.
The stated impact is nginx startup or config-validation failure followed by vigil-app container crashes and CrashLoopBackOff.

relationship.evidence: All diagnoses identify the invalid nginx directive in vigil-app-nginx-config as the sole root cause, directly causing startup failure and CrashLoopBackOff.

diagnosis_text:
Diagnosis 1:
 root_cause: The nginx ConfigMap `vigil-app-nginx-config` declares a bogus directive `invalid_directive on;` in the server block, so nginx exits with `[emerg] unknown directive` at startup, crashing and restart-looping the `vigil-app` container. This bad config is present in the git manifest, not injected at runtime. root_cause_component: ConfigMap/vigil-app-nginx-config → Deployment/vigil-app (container vigil-app, image nginx:stable)
